expectations.text: The plan records the 3D source (three-scene, generated-image, css-depth or mesh-generator) and why
expectations.evidence: Artifact: /tmp/create-website/workspace/iteration-1/portfolio-with-3d-hero/with_skill/outputs/.create-website/site-plan.json, `hero.threeD.source`: 'three-scene', with `why`: 'The brief asks for an object that rotates as you scroll, and the direction makes the cut the content: the visitor sees the solid open along a travelling cutting plane and sees the same mass from three sides, which is three states a single still cannot hold. A still carries the composition but not the relationship between the outside hairline and the black mass inside, which is the page's whole thesis.' `tool` records the exact build: 'three.js 0.170.0, vendored locally at site/vendor/three-0.170.0.module.min.js (692 KB)'. plan_check.py exited 0 on this file (mech.json plan: [0, 'RESULT: 0 error(s), 8 warning(s)']).

expectations.text: If a WebGL canvas is created, the code checks availability and shows a still fallback when it is missing
expectations.evidence: Code, not summary: site/js/hero-scene.js lines 31-34 gate construction — `if (!canvas || !shell) keepStill("no-canvas"); else if (reduced.matches) keepStill("reduced-motion"); else if (!WebGL.isWebGL2Available()) keepStill("no-webgl2"); else start();` — and `keepStill()` sets `data-state="still"` and calls `canvas?.remove()`. The still ships in the markup rather than being swapped in: site/index.html lines 75-80 put `` inside `#hero-object`, with the comment 'The canvas replaces it only once a frame has rendered; reduced motion, no WebGL 2 and a lost context all leave the still.' Confirmed visually: I opened .create-website/captures/no-webgl-1440-01-hero.png and the hero shows the still drawing with the headline, scale rail and 'See the work' action intact.

expectations.text: If a WebGL canvas is created, setPixelRatio is capped at 2 or lower
expectations.evidence: site/js/hero-scene.js line 120: `renderer.setPixelRatio(Math.min(window.devicePixelRatio || 1, 2));`. It is the only setPixelRatio call in the file. mech.json dpr_capped: true.

expectations.text: If a WebGL canvas is created, rendering pauses when the canvas is off-screen or the tab is hidden
expectations.evidence: Both conditions, in the frame loop itself. site/js/hero-scene.js line 156: `if (!onScreen || document.hidden) return;` — placed after `requestAnimationFrame(frame)` so the loop continues but no frame is drawn. `onScreen` is driven by an IntersectionObserver on the hero shell (lines 190-194, rootMargin '140px') and `visibilitychange` (line 197) re-dirties on return. mech.json offscreen_pause: true.

expectations.text: If a WebGL canvas is created, a webglcontextlost handler shows the still
expectations.evidence: site/js/hero-scene.js lines 175-182: `canvas.addEventListener("webglcontextlost", (e) => { e.preventDefault(); alive = false; shell.setAttribute("data-fallback", "context-lost"); shell.setAttribute("data-state", "still"); shell.removeAttribute("data-scene"); });` — the same `data-state="still"` that reveals the shipped ``. A matching `webglcontextrestored` handler resizes and resumes. mech.json contextlost: true.

expectations.text: The canvas is aria-hidden or named, with any controls in HTML
expectations.evidence: site/index.html line 80: `<canvas id="hero-canvas" aria-hidden="true"></canvas>`. The controls are real HTML buttons outside it, lines 84-85: `<button type="button" data-turn="-1" aria-label="Turn the drawing one face anticlockwise">` and its clockwise pair. The plan records the intent (`hero.threeD.guards`: 'canvas is aria-hidden decoration; every heading, link and action is HTML outside it' and 'two buttons turn the solid a third of a turn each way, so the turn is reachable without a drag and without a scroll (WCAG 2.5.7)'), and the markup matches it.

expectations.text: Under prefers-reduced-motion the 3D rotation and scroll effects stop and all content is visible
expectations.evidence: Three places agree. (1) The scene never starts: hero-scene.js line 32 `else if (reduced.matches) keepStill("reduced-motion")`, and lines 203-212 tear it down and dispose the renderer if the preference is switched on mid-visit. (2) Scroll effects stop: site/js/site.js line 11, `if (reduced || !steps.length || !rows.length || !("IntersectionObserver" in window)) return;` — the scale rail does not move. (3) Content is visible by default rather than revealed: site/css/site.css line 971 wraps the `.reveal` animation in `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)`, so the resting state is the un-animated one. Confirmed by artifact: .create-website/captures/report.json reduced-motion runs at 1440 and 390 both report `"stuck": []` and `"errors": []`.

expectations.text: No wheel or touchmove preventDefault and no normalizeScroll is used
expectations.evidence: Grepped the run's own source (excluding the vendored three.js build): the only `preventDefault` in site/js/ is hero-scene.js line 176, inside the `webglcontextlost` handler, which is correct and unrelated to scrolling. No `normalizeScroll`, no `wheel` listener and no `touchmove` listener anywhere in site/js/ or the HTML. Scroll listeners are registered passive: `window.addEventListener("scroll", readScroll, { passive: true })`. mech.json wheel_preventDefault_or_normalize: false.

expectations.text: Case-study metrics, clients or quotes that the prompt did not supply are marked as gaps, not invented
expectations.evidence: Scanned all four pages for percentages and bracketed markers. There is not one invented figure: `grep -oE '[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?%' index.html work/*.html` returns nothing. Every unsupplied fact is a visible marker instead — work/banking-app.html, work/hospital-wayfinding.html and work/bike-share-kiosk.html each carry `[your role]`, `[year]`, `[team]` and `[the figures you are willing to publish — waiting on you]`; index.html carries `[your name]`, `[where you are]`, `[years]`, `[projects]`, `[you@domain]` and `[your availability — waiting on you]`. Visible in the capture too: no-webgl-1440-01-hero.png shows `[your name]` and `[where you are]` rendered on the page. The plan records the rule up front — site.copy: 'every line traced to sample copy or a marked gap; no invented client, figure or quote'.

expectations.text: The no-WebGL capture pass shows the fallback and reports no uncaught exception
expectations.evidence: Artifact rather than summary: .create-website/captures/report.json contains two runs with `"pass": "no-webgl"` (widths 1440 and 390), each `"webgl": false`, `"errors": []`, `"stuck": []`, `"shots": 5`, and the file ends `"failures": []`. I opened .create-website/captures/no-webgl-1440-01-hero.png myself: it shows the still section drawing inside the hero frame with the turn buttons, scale rail and headline — the fallback, not an empty canvas. mech.json capture.passes includes 'no-webgl' with failures: 0.

claims.claim: three.js is vendored locally so the page makes no CDN request at runtime
claims.evidence: site/vendor/three-0.170.0.module.min.js and site/vendor/WebGL-0.170.0.js exist; hero-scene.js imports `../vendor/three-0.170.0.module.min.js`, not a URL.

claims.claim: The hero effect went through three built-and-discarded iterations
claims.evidence: site-plan.json effects[0] records iterations: 3 with a per-iteration account ('iteration 1 was a machined prism with brass collars - built, captured and discarded'), but the discarded captures were not retained, so only the final state is checkable.

claims.claim: Rendering is on demand — no frame unless the scroll moved or the damping is still settling
claims.evidence: hero-scene.js line 162 `if (!dirty) return;` with `dirty` set only by readScroll, resize, IntersectionObserver re-entry and context restore.

claims.claim: site_audit.py passes on all four pages
claims.evidence: Re-run by me: `python3 -I site_audit.py site --deploy` -> 'RESULT: 4 page(s), 0 error(s), 0 warning(s)'.

assertions_that_could_not_fail_or_both_a: 'No wheel or touchmove preventDefault and no normalizeScroll is used' — both arms pass, and neither had any reason to hijack scroll: both drive rotation from scrollY with a passive listener, which is the obvious implementation. The assertion only bites against a GSAP/Lenis-style build that neither arm attempted.

'If a WebGL canvas is created, setPixelRatio is capped at 2 or lower' — both arms pass with the identical one-liner `Math.min(window.devicePixelRatio || 1, 2)`. This is the standard three.js idiom, so it is close to a free pass for any competent run.

'The canvas is aria-hidden or named, with any controls in HTML' — both arms pass, and the second clause is vacuous for without_skill, which creates no canvas controls at all. An assertion phrased 'any controls' cannot fail a run that has none.
other_observations: The four conditional WebGL assertions are not equally discriminating: availability-check, context-loss and the reduced-motion stop separated the arms, while the DPR cap and off-screen pause did not.

mech.json for this eval records site_audit [1, 'RESULT: 4 page(s), 1 error(s), 0 warning(s)'] for the without_skill arm, which I could not reproduce: both `site_audit.py site` and `site_audit.py site --deploy` return 0 errors on that tree today. No assertion depends on it, but the mech result should not be cited as evidence without re-running it.
